The Phasmophobia community has raised more than $230,000 (around £173,000) for the American Heart Association, more than doubling last year's total.

Developer Kinetic Games announced the final figure for this year's Ghost Hunts for Hearts event on 6th November. The charity drive ran from 26th October to 2nd November, and more than 500 streamers signed up to take part. That's the biggest turnout yet for a creator fundraiser run by Heart Liive, the American Heart Association's streaming initiative.

Last year's event raised a little over $100,000.

Congratulations, Ghost Hunters, you've surpassed the community target and raised over $200,000 for our friends at @Heart_Liive!Your kindness and generosity will not go unrewarded, log in to Phasmophobia before the 15th November to claim the Animated AHA Advocate ID Card &… pic.twitter.com/KFQKaqXNCl

Streamers who fundraised could hand out an event-exclusive Advocate ID Card and Badge to their viewers as a Twitch Drop. Kinetic set a target of $200,000 at the start of the week, and once players sailed past it, an animated version of the card and badge set unlocked for all.

"The Phasmophobia community never fails to amaze us, and this year they've outdone themselves," said Tom Dent, lead social media and player experience manager at Kinetic Games. "Thank you to every streamer, viewer and player who took part."

Phasmophobia launched in Early Access in September 2020, and sends teams of up to four players into haunted locations to gather evidence of what's lurking there.

The studio also launched a publishing arm, Kinetic Publishing, earlier this year. Its first game, the starship job simulator Contact Protocol, is due out in spring 2027.

Phasmophobia is available in Early Access on Steam, PS5, PS VR2, and Xbox Series X/S. It's also coming to Nintendo Switch 2, although we still don't quite know when.

Earlier this year, Kinetic Games confirmed Phasmophobia's 1.0 launch had slipped from this year into 2027, as the studio said it was prioritising quality over speed following a rocky reception to its Player Character Update. The studio ended up apologising to players for issues with the long-awaited update, admitting it "missed the mark" and "didn't deliver on our promises to you".

Following Patrick Stewart's death, I'm still wrestling with the fact that the beloved actor is no longer with us. At the same time, though, I've also been enjoying the sweet and interesting anecdotes shared by those who've worked with him. With that, I was shocked to read a recently resurfaced story about Wil Wheaton apologizing to Stewart. It turned out the former child actor had some guilt about his behavior on the set of Star Trek: The Next Generation, and I'm not at all surprised to hear how Stewart responded.

The apology apparently came shortly after the end of production on 2002's Star Trek: Nemesis, which Wheaton was originally in before getting cut from the movie. Wheaton wrote in his book Just A Geek that he apologized to Stewart for his cocky behavior on the set of The Next Generation. After admitting he'd "been a dick" during filming, Wheaton wrote that the Picard actor said the following (via Star Trek Fan Group):

Wil, my dear, you were a teenager. We all understood… I wasn't thrilled about working with a child, but working with you was a great pleasure.

It's worth remembering that when Star Trek: The Next Generation first started, Wheaton was the biggest star of the bunch. The majority of audiences knew him through Rob Reiner's 1986 coming-of-age drama, Stand By Me, while Stewart and others were relative unknowns. This, paired with alleged emotional abuse at home, led Wheaton to have an arrogant attitude on set.

Wil Wheaton wouldn't open up about any of that until long after his time working on The Next Generation, and at this point, he's spoken about it at length. As Wheaton previously explained, the TNG cast was there for him when he felt his parents weren't, and he also saw Patrick Stewart as a father figure.

Stewart wrote about Wheaton on the set of TNG in his own memoir, Making It So. While the actor admitted feeling some annoyance at the young actor having such bravado, he ultimately realized it stemmed from his own insecurities as a lead in his breakout television role:

To me, he initially came off as cocky. But as I examined my feelings, I realized that they were not really about Wil or some notion that he should know his place as a juvenile actor — they reflected my own vulnerability. In those first weeks, I wished I had Wil’s confidence.

Wheaton shared a sweet throwback photo of him and Patrick Stewart shortly after news of the latter's death broke. It's great to know that, despite feeling like a "dick" for how he acted, Wheaton has such fond memories of that time and holds such a deep reverence for all of his cast members.

Stewart's death feels like a capstone on a year in which Star Trek's 60th anniversary has felt like a bittersweet celebration. His passing came just on the heels of fans mourning Walter Koenig, who played Pavel Chekov on the original series.

Take those two massive losses and the fact that there are no Star Trek shows in active development, and it's been a bit of a downer year. However, there is a movie in development as well as growing optimism that while Trek is in a valley, it may peak once again in the future. At present, though, I'm content with honoring Patrick Stewart for his contributions to Trek and for his character as human being.

Readers needing Star Trek in their lives can always stream the series on Paramount+, or for free over on Pluto TV. I've been streaming TNG in the wake of Stewart's death and have had a blast watching him in action.

#3774. Ocarina of Time remake datamine suggests Master Quest is on the way

Ocarina of Time's notoriously tricky Master Quest mode could be making a comeback in the new remake.

Dataminer MrCheeze shared a list of strings from the remake's files on Bluesky, several of which tie the tag "MQ" to dungeons like Dodongo's Cavern.

In a follow-up, as spotted by TheGamer, they pointed to further entries, including "HasMQ", "IsMQModeExist", "NewGameMQ", and "ReleaseMQ".

Fellow dataminer OatmealDome added on Twitter/X that the mode will be unlocked by owning DLC, rather than arriving in an update, though "the data is incomplete". "I can confirm that the world is mirrored and dungeons are modified (e.g. cows in Jabu-Jabu's Belly)," they said.

If you've not played it, Master Quest is a remixed version of Ocarina of Time with rearranged dungeons and tougher puzzles. It first appeared as a bonus disc on GameCube, then came back in 2011's Ocarina of Time 3D, which unlocked it after you finished the main game. That version also mirrored the whole world, which matches what OatmealDome has found, and had enemies deal double damage.

[Ocarina of Time] #ootspoilersThere is data in the game files for Master Quest. It will be unlocked by *owning DLC* - it is not just an update.The data is incomplete, but I can confirm that the world is mirrored and dungeons are modified (e.g. cows in Jabu-Jabu's Belly).

As with any datamine, there's no guarantee it'll ever see the light of day. Nintendo hasn't announced any DLC for the remake, and it's not clear whether Master Quest would be free, like it was on 3DS, or paid.

The Ocarina of Time remake launched on Switch 2 on 5th November. Donlan called the new version an "astonishing remake" in his five-star Eurogamer Ocarina of Time review.

Though, to be honest, sometimes I want to play someone else's game.

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

Skyrim lead designer Bruce Nesmith had a wide-ranging chat with The Examined Game recently, touching upon topics like the importance of institutional knowledge, what he liked about Baldur's Gate 3, and what he wants to see in The Elder Scrolls 6: Sentinel. But he also dropped a pithy maxim (and less pithy explanation) about his—and Bethesda's—approach to design in general. Here's what he said.

"If you look at the history of triple-A studios that do sequels… you'll see the best game in a sequence frequently was able to maintain a vision, and was very player-centric-forward: 'You're not playing my game, I'm making your game' kind of thing.

One of the things I've always felt, and [Bethesda] felt it too [is] once we've made a game, it's not ours anymore. It's yours. I, once upon a time, actually had a developer complain to me that the people playing his game—it wasn't anything Bethesda produced—were playing it wrong.

I immediately told him, 'they're not playing it wrong, they cannot play it wrong, it's their game. It's not yours anymore. However they are choosing to play it is the right way to play it'... If you embrace that on the developer side, you find yourself making all different kinds of content, both artistically and design, and for programming in terms of the systems that are available, so that everyone can play the game the way they want to".

I'm not sure I've ever heard a more succinct summation of the Bethesda school of game design than "You're not playing my game, I'm making your game". Accessibility, openness, a sanding down of edges that may scare off the normies (like ability scores and character classes—gone but not forgotten), and a general refusal to foreclose story branches or quest chains based on player decisions: these things are Bethesda to me.

In this maxim you find all the strengths and weaknesses of the studio's approach to open-world RPG design. On the one hand, the world is your oyster. If a questline is losing your interest, flip to another one. Don't like your build? Convert to something new. Bethesda's worlds are all-you-can-eat buffets and you have precisely zero dietary restrictions. True freedom!

And yet, and yet, to a certain kind of tedious grognard (me), it also leaves everything feeling a touch… limp—colourless in content and utterly unresponsive. You might be the head of every guild in the land and the bloodletter-in-chief of the local murder society, but the world is too shy to reply to it. After all, it can't. If your choices impacted things too hard you might experience a consequence, you might rub up against a rough edge, and then suddenly you might not be playing "your" game anymore.

#3772. GTA 6 party continues with Travis Scott, Cardi B, and more while you’ll be at home playing the game

Real world parties for an open world game.

It’s hard to believe, but Grand Theft Auto 6 is finally coming out next week, and Rockstar Games and PlayStation are throwing another big party in its honor.

Today, the companies announced GTA 6: The Festival, a special live concert at a convention center in Miami that’s “featuring a star-studded lineup of artists from the game and the official soundtrack,” including Travis Scott, Cardi B, Metro Boomin, and more, like French DJ duo Justice, who scored the game’s soundtrack.

Grand Theft Auto VI: The Festival, a special live event on November 21 at Mana Wynwood in Miami to celebrate the launch of GTAVI, featuring a star-studded lineup of artists from the game and the official soundtrack.More info: https://t.co/XRlfYFOk0H pic.twitter.com/fQyOU7I4gU

“This is a one-of-a-kind launch event that features two stages of nonstop music,” the website teases, confirming that entrants need to be 17 or older, and getting tickets means winning a literal lottery that will be drawn tomorrow at 6pm CT.

This sounds fun, and I’m sure it’ll be a great time, but I’m not really sure who the target demographic is for this sort of event. It’s definitely not GTA 6 players, right? Because when the event takes place next Saturday, Nov. 21, we’ll all be in Vice City playing through Jason and Lucia’s story as opposed to clubbing it up. Plus, can’t we just go to nightclubs in the game instead, and not have to deal with brain-pounding music, sweating profusely, and weird smells all around us?

I shouldn’t speak for all gamers, but I feel like I’m justified in saying that. GTA fans have been waiting over 13 years for this game, so while one night out feels like nothing in comparison, I think we’d all rather be playing the game itself, especially on its first weekend.

This is just another wildly outrageous form of advertising for GTA 6, which already has takeovers planned for the Miami Heat game on Nov. 18, the E11EVEN Miami nightclub turning into its Vice City counterpart, NINE1NINE Vice City, for a whole month, and a whole lot more.

You can read more about GTA 6: The Festival on Rockstar Games’ website, which is also filled with a slew of awesome screenshots of the actual game.

Stallone isn't exactly the easiest man to impress.

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

While the 1976 film Rocky tells the story of an underdog fighter, the biopic about the making of Rocky reveals the equally fascinating underdog story behind the Oscar-winning film's development. Through Peter Farrelly's I Play Rocky, audiences see see the inspirational story chronicling young Sylvester Stallone's aim to play the lead boxer in the film (which he wrote). As for the real Stallone's thoughts on the film, he admitted to having been ready to be “hypercritical” of it. However, that changed after he saw the film.

In I Play Rocky, Anthony Ippolito plays young Sylvester Stallone, and he's the spitting image of the Rocky icon. Based on the trailers alone, Ippolito completely nails the Rambo actor’s voice and swagger. Still, I'd imagine that the biggest stamp of approval would come from Stallone himself. After the Cobra actor saw the biopic, he admitted to CBS Mornings that he was somewhat reluctant about the 2026 movie release, but even he eventually gave into it:

It was very surreal because at first I was gonna be hypercritical, like that's me. I don't walk like that. But I did walk like that. I did talk like that. I'm realizing this guy did a magnificent job, and I actually forgot I was me, and I sat back and watched the movie like the audience.

I can understand Stallone's natural inclination to be “hypercritical,” especially given this is his story being told. It must be trippy for him to see another actor channel his voice and mannerisms and emulate his role as Rocky Balboa. However, it’s a relief that the Expendables star has high praise for the biopic and Ippolito himself. I know I keep harping on it, but seriously, it's hard to deny how accurately Ippolito takes on Stallone's baritone voice and rugged physical presence.

The Tulsa King star isn’t the only one loving I Play Rocky. Early reviews were quick to give praise, with many saying Ippolito fully absorbed Stallone so much that someone could forget it was a performance. Ryan Gosling also gave his stamp of approval, telling lead female actress Annasophia Robb how much he loved it. With all of these rave reviews, I’d say Stallone is right on the mark.

During his CBS Mornings interview, Stallone also said that if Ippolito didn’t endure a concussion during his I Play Rocky training, then he “didn’t try hard enough” with the role. Well, Ippolito said -- after being shown the footage of Stallone's chat -- that he may not have gotten a concussion, but he did get “a little banged up” training at the historic Gleason’s Gym. So, we can’t say the Offer actor didn’t put in the grunt work like Stallone did when he first played “The Italian Stallion.”

It's not small feat for an actor to play such a recognizable star like Sylvester Stallone, so Anthony Ippolito deserves some serious credit. And, if Stallone felt like he was watching himself while watching the movie, I have a feeling audiences will also be engaged.

Right now, I Play Rocky is playing in limited release, but the film will open nationwide on November 20. Also, fans can also relive Balboa's exploits by streaming the Rocky movies with a Paramount+ subscription.

Just your average South Floridian cinephile who believes the pen is mightier than the sword.

#3770. COD: Modern Warfare 4 gets a surprisingly sudden free trial, so you can see what the game's extraction mode DMZ is like

Activision has released the first trial for Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4's extraction mode DMZ. The trial is available across PC (Steam / Battlenet), PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X/S until Wednesday, 11th November.

The free trial only includes access to DMZ and no other part of Modern Warfare 4, such as multiplayer or the campaign. And while it's not uncommon for Call of Duty titles to make some of their modes available for free for a limited time, the timing of this DMZ taster is notable.

DMZ launched days before Modern Warfare 4's 23rd October release date, meaning this first trial has arrived just two weeks after the game's full launch. By comparison, Black Ops 7's Endgame mode had its first free trial months after launch, in the game's third season. That said, Endgame continued to be freely available until Season 6.

The DMZ trial also coincides with the launch of Modern Warfare 4's iteration of free-to-play Call of Duty battle royale mode Warzone, and Season 1. Indeed, both DMZ and the new Warzone take place on the same Hajin map, so even if you don't decide to buy the full game to continue playing DMZ, some of that map knowledge will certainly transfer to Warzone.

The DMZ trial does not appear to have any limits, meaning you can climb the ranks, access Story Missions - the only way to play PvE, with caveats - and complete Orders to your heart's content. That includes X01, the new endgame dungeon-like area available to experienced and fully-equipped players.

DMZ players who've been asking Infinity Ward to offer a PvE-only playlist of the PvPvE mode will certainly be happy with the influx of new players, as they could potentially amplify their calls for a PvP-free playlist.

Last weekend was Halloween. A night for creeps. An evening of shrieks. For some scream queen royalty, they got one of the more unpleasant kinds of frights. This came to the surprise to the original cast, who were attached to star in the follow-up. Instead it seems Driscoll opted to use AI to generate the film, leaving fans and alumni more aghast at him than the flesh eating ghouls.

“This is not what we signed up for,” says Beverly Randolph on the Caffeinated Horror Dude podcast. “We got to get something out there because there’s so much hate on us right now.”

Due to some erroneous paperwork, George A. Romeroâs original Night of the Living Dead was released directly into the public domain in 1968. Because of this, it enabled any director and studio, including Romero himself, to develop âsequelsâ to the series regardless of legal claim. One of the more adored successors is Return of the Living Dead, where a gang of punk teenagers take refuge in a morgue after a melting brain eater escapes containment. It has since stood on its own as a cult classic, generating its own sequels. This includes Brian Yuznaâs grotesque Return of the Living Dead 3, which I mostly bring up because it scared the shit out of me as a kid.

In 2024, Driscoll, who operates his own no-budget streaming service “DragonFLIX,” launched an Indiegogo page for “TRASH’s REVENGE Return of the Living Dead Universe.” Unlike other fan projects, this one had a large portion of the original cast involved, with stars Randolph and Linnea Quigley acting as producers. It also threw in Quigleyâs fellow Sorority Babe in the Slimeball Bowl-O-Rama Michelle Bauer and the Oscar nominated Eric Roberts, who has seemingly been in everything except The Living Dead.

From what Quigley described, this movie was intended to be a blend of Sunset Boulevard and Rocky Horror. Trash, Quigleyâs character who was last seen as a nudist zombie, had become a Norma Desmond recluse, relishing in the glory days of her brain eating spree. This sounds incredible. But after some confusion and radio silence between the cast and director, this incredible movie did not come to be.

Last Halloween night, Driscoll pushed out The Return of the Living Dead: Aftermath, an almost entirely AI generated heap of rotting flesh. The results wonât surprise you. Robotic line delivery. Nonsensical sequence of events. Object impermanence. Everythingâs wet. Everyone looks shocked. At one point the video just flips around like youâre watching on a phone someone dropped. And while the Return cast didnât film any of this footage, their likenesses are peppered throughout.

“It turned out to be a fiasco,” says Quigley. “I warned him, “Whatever you do, donât do any AI, because people donât like it, the fans donât like it.””

Living Dead alumni, even those who werenât attached to this film, have spoken out against Aftermath. They seem most concerned about the existing and continued use of their likeness, given that Driscoll has seemingly pivoted ‘Trashâs Revenge’ into an additional project. Randolph encourages those who provided any funding to ask for a refund through their credit card company. While Romeroâs original film was public domain, Return was not. Randolph also encourages Amazon, who bought MGM in 2022, to take legal action.

A short video posted on Rivals social media accounts this morning shows Jeff the Landshark dodging enemy attacks as he disappears in a puff of purple smoke with the word “BAMF!” popping up within. Even casual Marvel fans will quickly pick up that this means X-Men member Nightcrawler is set to arrive as the game’s next playable hero.

Not this time! Looks like Jeff has someone watching over him…🤫 pic.twitter.com/JEoAr7AmBt

Season 11 of Marvel Rivals begins this Friday, which means we’ll likely have a rollout of info on Nightcrawler and what to expect in the season coming over the next few days (he’s rumored to be a Strategist). But Nightcrawler’s confirmation lends a lot of legitimacy to yet another round of leaks regarding new hero releases.

Months ago, data miners found that Nightcrawler and Dr. Doom (rumored to be a dual Vanguard and Duelist hero) would be joining the roster in season 11, but new information found over the weekend shows a plethora if additional additions to the playable gallery are coming in 2027, with the aforementioned duo also included in that list.

A leaker posted a list of starred out characters teasing who’s coming in 2027, and players quickly put the pieces together to estimate that the list includes Dazzler, Dracula, Spider-Gwen, Green Goblin, Bishop, Cable, Miles Morales, Misty Knight, Captain Marvel, Vision, and Clea are next up

Noted Rivals leaker MultiverSusie said that the list making the rounds is “90 percent” correct, but “it’s missing a specific character” to which they posted a skull and fire emoji, so they are essentially saying Ghost Rider is missing from the list and also coming soon.

I admittedly have not played Rivals in quite some time, as the solo experience hasn’t been fun for a while, and the game’s constant additions of new heroes creates a balancing mess. The community of players is not all that great, either, but I will always be interested in seeing what Marvel heroes will come up next as I’m always going to be a fan of the IP. And as Nightcrawler is my favorite X-Men member, I will have to download it and give the hero a shot again.

We should know more tomorrow when NetEase begins teasing season 11.

Last Friday, the very good RPG Nier: Automata underwent what the scientific community calls 'puffer-fishification'. That is to say, it suddenly and inexplicably ballooned to over 700% of its original download size, as an update magically transformed the game from a reedy 50 GB lightweight into a 366-GB behemoth.

But it has since hit the Ozempic and is now back down to its regular size. "We have identified the cause and now resolved this issue," tweeted the official Nier X account earlier today. "Apologies for any inconvenience caused."

Notably absent from the bugfix notice was any explanation as to just what had happened. It might be academic at this point, but I for one would love to know how you accidentally make a game seven times bigger without anything changing.

Squenix is keeping schtum, but Rick Lane suggested, in our article last week about the bug, that it might have been related to Nier: Automata's DLC packages. "When selected for download on Steam, each DLC appears to have the same file size as the base game", he noted. "Weirdly though, this is only true for the initial download and installation. Once the game is installed, the file reportedly reverts to a more appropriate size of roughly 50 gigs." Indeed, the suggested temporary workaround for the issue (before Square Enix fixed it) was to uncheck all the DLCs when you installed the game.

So it sure seems like, somehow, the base files for the entire original game got attached to each individual DLC package. That might also explain why the size increase only applied to the downloads and not its install size—the whole game got downloaded eight times, but it was simply overwriting the base game files over and over.

That's just my speculation though, and without more news from Squenix, that's all we're gonna get. For now, enjoy being able to once again download 2B and 9S' adventures without having to start the download two weeks in advance.

#3766. GTA 6 reportedly has 55 Achievements/Trophies, more than both GTA 5 and Red Dead Redemption 2 had at launch

GTA 6 is due to release on the 19th November on PS5, and Xbox Series X/S, and ahead of the highly-anticipated launch of Rockstar's latest sandbox adventure, people just can't get enough information about the game. To that end, overnight, we saw our latest leak: the game will have 55 Trophies/Achievements.

In a now-deleted tweet from (in)famous Rockstar dataminer, TexFunz2 - re-posted by the Twitter account iGrandTheftAuto - it appears the game will have 55 individual rewards for completing certain tasks and missions. At the time of writing, we don't know specifically what these challenges are, but it seems none of them will be attached to the online version of the game; the base game launches without GTA Online, and so we can safely assume that all these rewards will be for the single-player only content. GTA Online will drop sometime in 2027, according to Twitch's CEO.

If you've been paying attention to previous Rockstar titles, you'll know that Grand Theft Auto 5 launched with 51 Achievements/Trophies - again, all single-player - and Red Dead Redemption 2 launched with 52. So the latest game has more than either game got at launch - and I can tell you from experience, getting Platinum in either title was a very time-consuming experience. Expect the same to be true here, too.

It's worth highlighting that GTA 5 did, eventually, get more Achievements and Trophies: the GTA Online content upped the complete total to 78, adding 27 new challenges to complete. I would expect GTA 6 to do the same… whenever the PC version of GTA comes out, or GTA Online lands in the new game (it's possible both could happen at the same time).

Carson Daly has long been one of the hardest working people in show business, and that’s continued amid the 2026 TV schedule. He’s still been fulfilling his obligations to The Today Show and, at the same time, he’s remained the host of The Voice amid Season 30. This past week, though, it was announced that Daly would take on a new Today job, as he’s officially been named the co-anchor of the show’s Saturday broadcast. With that, Blake Shelton, Riley Green and other Voice coaches shared their reactions to the news.

For a little while now, Daly had been pulling double duty on Today, serving as a features anchor/co-host during the week and serving as co-anchor on Saturdays. November 7 actually marked his first official day as co-anchor of Today Saturday alongside Laura Jarrett. Fans had hoped Daly might land the gig, and they seem excited now that he has. They’re not the only ones, as Today shared a video in which Green, Shelton, Kelly Clarkson and Adam Levine all congratulated Daly. Check it out:

It’s so sweet that the Voice coaches would take time to send such supportive messages to Daly, who’s been hosting the reality competition series since its debut in 2011. What’s even funnier to me is that each comment feels on brand for the person sharing it. For instance, I’m not surprised that Clarkson would share such bubbly sentiments:

Carson Daly, congratulations on getting Saturday on Today! People love you. They just want your face all the time. I do.

Of course, Shelton and Daly have long had a friendly rivalry filled with occasional trolling. So, while Shelton’s message to his longtime pal and former co-star is sweet, it also features a couple of funny jabs:

Man, just wanted to drop a line here and say congratulations on the Saturday Today Show. I think you’re going to do an incredible job. I’m not too worried about it, because I know Saturday’s like any other day of the week for you. You’ll be drinking. And I know you’ll do a great job, you’ll feel natural. Maybe because it’s the weekend show, it’ll be more entertainment, not as much breaking news, which is good for you, because I don’t think people take you that seriously anyway. Anyway, buddy, good luck. Love you.

All of these warm thoughts come on the heels of rumors regarding Daly possibly leaving The Voice, on which he also serves as an executive producer. The Daly speculation proved to be correct and incorrect, as he did return for Season 30 but was confirmed to not be hosting Season 31. That latter season is subtitled Celebrity and will not only bring a new format to the franchise but will also see Keke Palmer take over hosting duties from Daly.

Considering Palmer’s presence and the potential for Carson Daly’s role on The Today Show to grow with this new job, it’s hard not to wonder whether he might step away from The Voice for good. Daly himself hasn’t given any indication that he plans to leave, as of this writing. Fans will just have to wait and see how that all plays out but, for now, let’s take a page out of the Voice coaches’ book and congratulate Daly on his new position!

#3764. Dungeons in World of Warcraft: Forever get a huge XP buff, but power-levellers shouldn't celebrate just yet

World of Warcraft: Forever has received a massive buff to the XP drop-rates of dungeon mobs (enemies), which should make running these instances multiple times feel more rewarding - and may revive an older levelling strategy.

This buff is a 50 percent increase in experience from all mobs killed inside all dungeons. As detailed in this World of Warcraft forum post, community manager Kaivax wrote that this change has been made "so it feels better to go back in for more runs". They don't outright say this is in response to community feedback, but the subject has been a hot topic since the beta.

World of Warcraft: Forever developers have spoken in the past about the decision to deliberately bring down dungeon mob XP to disincentivise power-levelling in dungeons. The idea was that by doing this, people would be encouraged to actually go out into the world and explore it, rather than hopping from instance to instance until they reached max level.

Sadly, a side effect of this change is that doing a dungeon more than once could feel unrewarding. Playing it once is great, as you get to complete lots of quests that reward guaranteed items and XP. However, if you go back again, you don't get these, so your only source of progression comes from a heavily decreased XP rate.

Some quests exacerbate this issue. Dungeons like Wailing Caverns and especially Blackfathom Deeps have a quest that can't really be completed in one run due to a reliance on drop rates for items you need, and having to fight for drops with the rest of your dungeon party. Having to go back to complete this used to suck, and now it sucks less!

So does this mean farming dungeons to power-level is back? Maybe, but it still won't be nearly as efficient as it was in older versions of Classic WoW. The current mob XP rates, after this buff, will still only be 36 percent of the original Classic rate - a third. Given how fast you can level by doing quests out in the world, it seems dungeon farming isn't due for a comeback just yet.

After an especially smooth launch, World of Warcraft: Forever has become the biggest launch in the series' history, beating out Wrath of the Lich King, Cataclysm, and all the other past expansion launches. The developers have been quick to hotfix things on the fly, including a change that left PvP battlegrounds heavily advantaged for the Horde.

I've spent far too much of my life covering the rampant ascent of AI. A juggernaut of tech development, destined to change the world into some sort of sci-fi utopia (if you believe its advocates) or fated to come crashing down around our ears, taking a large chunk of the world economy with it. Or the end of the world as we know it, according to some.

And now, the pillars upon which the AI revolution sits seem to be shaking beneath it. The most recent tremors began with the wobbling of US AI-led tech stocks in mid-October, after a similar descent in China earlier this year. Then at the end of the month, while many tech companies reported huge amounts of revenue in their quarterly financial results, some AI tech share prices still slid under a black cloud of investor doubt.

None more so than Alphabet, the owner of Google. A $500 billion wipe in stock price, led by the admission that the company's own AI search features were eating into its ad revenue, rocked the market. A wider tech sell-off, fuelled by fears regarding the eventual profitability of AI and a potential upcoming Democrat victory in the US midterms, rattled the valuations of many AI tech companies—alongside the chip manufacturers sitting underneath them.

All this, of course, amid a backdrop of increasing AI-related concerns across multiple fields. Rogue AI agents. Increasing AI-powered cybersecurity incidents. Predictions of the end of civilisation, brought on by rampant AI development without proper oversight. Fears of job market ruination. AI psychosis. The list goes on.

Then, the so-called blue wave came to pass. Democrats won control of both the US House and the Senate. Such sweeping political changes can rarely be ascribed to a single factor, but US voter polling indicates that data center expansion was a key source of voter frustration. The current Republican administration has gone all in on AI, and much of the US public seems displeased at the idea of massive AI tech facilities springing up left, right, and center across the country.

Jensen Huang has hit the headlines over allegations surrounding his involvement with an alleged Chinese spy.

Trillions were wiped off US tech stock values as investors sold off increasing numbers of shares in tech companies, amid further fears that the great AI infrastructure buildout was about to be reigned in by political changes. Long-called-for regulation of AI and AI companies seemed—and indeed, still seems—ever more likely.

And now, Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang has hit the headlines over allegations surrounding his involvement with an alleged Chinese spy. At first, it was reported that Alice Huang (no relation) had a "close relationship" with the Nvidia chief.

Keep up to date with the most important stories and the best deals, as picked by the PC Gamer team.

Now, Jensen Huang has himself admitted that the two were engaged in an affair, and Nvidia has launched an internal investigation into concerns related to national security. The timing could not be worse for the US tech market. At the time of writing, Nvidia's share value has sunk in pre-market trading.

The company is, in many ways, the backbone of the AI revolution, the chief provider of the chips behind the sweeping AI rollout that has changed the tech landscape over the past few years, and the creator of the CUDA platform that underpins it. Huang is its charismatic leader, the relentless optimist behind this AI-led future we're supposedly about to enjoy. A scandal at this stage is likely the last thing any tech investor wants to see.

So, what now? While the long-mooted AI bubble burst has yet to materialise in full, it's certainly looking like the relentless "all the money in the world" optimism phase is coming to an end. Investors are shaken, with worries about long-term profitability continuing to eat into the market, alongside US national security concerns now dominating the headlines.

The train with no brakes is rocking wildly against the tracks—and unfortunately, given AI and big tech's role in the global economy, we're all stuck in the carriages behind it.

The relentless "all the money in the world" optimism phase is coming to an end.

I'm no economist. I can't tell you if this is the beginning of the AI bubble pop, or whether this is merely an extremely turbulent time in the AI success story. Certainly, it seems like the horse has already bolted, and that AI is here to stay in some form or fashion. Those hoping for a return to the good old, pre-AI days are almost certain to be disappointed.

But, having reported on so many "AI doomsayers" over the past few years, I can tell you that a fall from grace has been predicted by many. Such a massive, world-changing technological development, fuelled by seemingly impossible amounts of investment, has always seemed destined to face some sort of financial reckoning.

That reckoning, I believe, has never looked closer. May you live in interesting times, as the old saying goes. And what happens next? Well, it's going to be interesting, at the very least.
